sw_oldfisher.text: In my day we fished the Minch for herring: hundreds of boats at the quay, and the herring girls travelling round the coast gutting for twelve hours a day. They sang and they were fast. Faster than the knife, some of them.

I met a Blue Man once. I was fourteen, in a boat in a thick fog, and a wee voice said a rhyme. I got it wrong, mind. I swam ashore. The rhyme was 'Skipper, skipper, mind the rocks'. I said 'Aye'. It's not in the right metre.
